punchline: Seneca quotes the plan "after my fiftieth year I'll retire to leisure" and answers: how late it is to begin living just when life must end.
thirty_sec: Augustus spent years praying for rest from the business of state. Seneca says ordinary people plan the same rest for their fifties and sixties, and his answer is blunt: how late it is to begin living just when life must end. He calls expectancy, relying on tomorrow, the greatest impediment to living, and urges his friend Paulinus, who runs the grain supply, to withdraw while he still can.
